Draft:

Dear Principal,

I am writing about your decision on whether all students should be required to perform community service. I believe you should not make it mandatory, but you should make it much easier and more rewarding for students to volunteer.

I understand why a requirement sounds appealing. Some of my friends tutor elementary school children, and they come back from those afternoons proud and energized. Others spend Saturdays picking up litter at the park, and the park really does look better afterward. These students care about their town, and their work shows how much a community gains when young people pitch in.

However, the same service can feel very different when it is forced. Many of my classmates already juggle homework, sports, part-time jobs, and caring for younger siblings. One friend of mine works evenings at a grocery store to help her family pay rent. Adding a mandatory number of service hours would give her one more thing to squeeze in, and she would likely resent it. A student who volunteers only to check a box often does the bare minimum, and the people being helped can tell the difference between someone who wants to be there and someone who has to be.

There is also a practical problem. Tutoring and cleanups need supervision and planning. If hundreds of students must find placements at once, the school and local groups could be overwhelmed, and some students would end up with busywork that helps no one.

A better plan would be to encourage service rather than demand it. The school could host a volunteer fair where local organizations recruit students, offer recognition at assemblies for those who serve, and allow service to be done in flexible ways, such as during school-sponsored events. Students who discover something they enjoy will keep serving long after graduation.

Thank you for considering my views. I hope our school will inspire students to help their community, not just require it.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
